Bug_Title: Eq: equals method compares class names rather than class objects (EQ_COMPARING_CLASS_NAMES)
Bug_Details:
This class defines an equals method that checks to see if two objects are the same class by checking to see if the names
of their classes are equal. You can have different classes with the same name if they are loaded by
different class loaders. Just check to see if the class objects are the same.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by implementing the equals method to compare the class names using getClass().getName() instead of comparing the class objects directly using getClass() == obj.getClass().
Trigger_Explanation: The testEqualsWithSameClassNamesButDifferentObjects test case creates two instances of ClassNameEqualityBug with different names. It then calls the showBug method on one instance, passing the other instance as an argument. The showBug method internally calls the equals method, which incorrectly compares the class names using getClass().getName() instead of comparing the class objects directly using getClass() == obj.getClass(). Since both objects are instances of the same class, the class names are the same, causing the equals method to return true, which is incorrect.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results show that the test passed without any assertion errors, indicating that the 'equals' method returned 'true' when comparing two objects of the same class but with different content. However, according to the bug description, the equals method should return 'false' for different objects even if they belong to the same class. Since the test does not fail, it suggests that the bug was not triggered as expected in this specific test case.
